_provenance: Built by scripts/build_cycle_index.py from data/lectionary/days/2025.json through 2036.json (12 civil-year files). The Epistle and Gospel streams of the post-Pentecost windows (day after Pentecost to the end of each civil year, within one file) were merged SEPARATELY — never as (epistle, gospel) pairs, since the two cycles are independent sequences that decouple after the Lukan jump. Each stream's 12 per-year ordered ref lists were sorted longest-first and folded into one stable order-preserving union (Epistle union = 214 refs, Gospel union = 216). after-pentecost labels are derived from the SOURCE DATA, never from union position: apostolos slots use the strict-majority verbatim cycle string across the 12 years (full tally in label_sources); evangelion slots take the day name from the strict-majority real weekday of the source days (tally in label_sources) and number the week within the Gospel block (Matthew restarts at week 1, Mark continues the Matthew count, Luke restarts at week 1), with a matthew/mark/luke block for book headings. Pentecostarion and Triodion slots are grouped by verbatim cycle label across all 12 years, each grouped day split into its Epistle slot (apostolos part) and Gospel slot (evangelion part); no-liturgy Lenten weekdays keep a has_liturgy=false slot with their 6th-Hour/Vespers readings under oldtestament in BOTH parts, so the two halves stay day-for-day comparable; triodion labels with an Epistle but no Gospel carry a note recording that no plain Gospel reading exists on those days in any of the 12 source years.
